# Jambot Full Review — 2026-07-27

187-agent audit (DSP render-testing of every instrument and effect, architecture-hygiene review against the repo's own docs, model audit), every finding adversarially verified by an independent agent. **168 findings raised, 166 confirmed, 2 refuted.**

## Fixed in this pass (commit accompanying this report)

1. **jb202 screech (critical)** — additive env→cutoff (`base + env*8000`, accent env velocity 1.5) pinned the filter at 5-16kHz on accents. Ported the jt30 exponential octave mapping (bipolar-safe, 5.5kHz cap, accent = 1.25× octave boost). Measured after: HF>5k energy 0.0% at res 85 / envMod 100; loudest line above 2.5k = -55.8 dBFS.
2. **jt10 static-resonance whistle (critical)** — envResCap only protected envelope sweeps; static high cutoff + high res self-oscillated. Now: exponential env mapping + resonance damping that follows the actual cutoff. After: HF>5k 0.5%, loudest line -46 dBFS at cutoff 12k / res 100.
3. **jt30 residual cap-whistle (major)** — ladder feedback damping now bites at the 5.5kHz engine cap (r ≤ 2.4 at res 100 there), squelch below 1.5kHz untouched. After: maxed 100/100/100 settings measure -39.8 dBFS worst line, HF 0.1%.
4. **jp9000 filter-lp24 clipping (critical)** — +19dB uncompensated resonance gain hard-clipped normal patches; added resonance-scaled output compensation.
5. **Model (critical)** — agent loop was pinned to retired `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` (404s since June 15). Now `process.env.JAMBOT_MODEL || "claude-opus-5"`; set `JAMBOT_MODEL=claude-fable-5` for the top-tier model. dist/ rebundled.
6. **Infinite-loop guard (major)** — any stop_reason other than end_turn/tool_use re-sent the identical request forever (billing loop); loop now terminates with a message.

All 32 architecture tests pass after the fixes.

## Not fixed — prioritized backlog (verified findings)


### Critical (16)

- **[dsp-screech] `web/public/jb202/dist/machines/jb202/engine.js` L220** — The additive envelope-to-cutoff mapping (base + envAmount*env*8000, clamp 16000) combined with the accent filter-env trigger velocity of 1.5 (line 128) pins the filter at base+12000 Hz on every accented note at high envMod, turning the bass synth into near-full-scale 5-16 kHz buzz — the exact disease fixed in jt30 on 2026-07-26.
  - Fix: Port the jt30 fix (jt30 engine.js ~lines 220-245): exponential octave-based mapping — shape the env (env*env), modCutoff = clamp(baseCutoff * 2^(envAmount * 4.5 * env^2 * accentBoost), 20, 5500) with accent as a 1.25x octave boost, and drop the 1.5 filter-env trigger velocity back to 1.0 (keep amp accent as-is). envAmount is bipolar here, and the exponential form handles negative amounts naturally.
- **[dsp-screech] `web/public/jt10/dist/machines/jt10/engine.js` L276** — With envMod low, high static cutoff plus high resonance self-oscillates into a whistle that buries the note by 14-23 dB, because the envResCap protects only envelope-driven sweeps (it scales with params.envMod, not with the actual cutoff).
  - Fix: Make the resonance damping depend on the actual modCutoff each sample (e.g. cappedResonance *= max(1 - k*(modCutoff/16000)^2, floor)) instead of the envMod knob, or clamp modCutoff/base cutoff to ~5.5-8 kHz as the jt30 fix does; alternatively strengthen the moog-ladder damping term for fc 0.3-0.75 where r=2.17 still rings at -8 dBFS.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/voices/lowtom.js` L86** — The tom soft-clip WaveShaper curve maps zero input to -0.00586 instead of 0, so every scheduled-but-not-yet-played tom hit leaks constant DC at full pre-trigger gain, putting a DC pedestal under any pattern containing toms that scales with hit count.
  - Fix: Generate a symmetric odd-length curve so curve(0)=0: `const samples = 257; const x = (i/(samples-1))*2 - 1;` in createSoftClipCurve of both lowtom.js (line 82-90) and hitom.js (line 74-82, same expression at hitom.js:78). Verified in the repro to eliminate the leak exactly.
- **[dsp-screech] `web/public/jp9000/dist/modules/filter-lp24.js` L34** — filter-lp24 resonance adds up to +19 dB of uncompensated gain, hard-clipping the render at completely normal settings including the shipped 'basic' preset.
  - Fix: Use the fixed MoogLadderFilter instead of Lowpass24Filter, or add gain compensation in Lowpass24Filter._updateCoefficients (scale output by ~1/(q1*q2) at resonance, matching moog-ladder.js's compensation) plus a soft-clip on the stage output.
- **[dsp-other] `instruments/jbs-node.js` L113** — Every JB-S per-slot parameter set via the generic tweak tool is unit-converted twice (tweak's toEngine at generic-tools.js:118, then getSlotEngineParams' toEngine again), so all slot tweaks produce drastically wrong audio: filter collapses to 200 Hz for any value, decay/attack collapse to ~1% of range, pan and level become inert.
  - Fix: Make the units consistent on one side: either have JBSNode.setParam accept/store engine units and have getSlotEngineParams pass stored values through without re-converting (converting only registered defaults once), or route jbs.* slot paths through the same producer-units skip that 'isNodeLevel' uses in generic-tools.js tweak so setParam receives producer units matching its clamp range and the single toEngine in getSlotEngineParams.
- **[dsp-other] `sample-voice.js` L66** — Tune is a three-state switch, not a pitch control: toEngine emits cents (semitones*100) but SampleVoice.setParameter('tune') interprets the value as semitones and clamps to [-12,+12], so any positive tune snaps to exactly +12 st and any negative to -12 st.
  - Fix: Make SampleVoice.trigger interpret the engine value as cents: clamp to [-2400, 2400] and use Math.pow(2, cents/1200) (or have the jbs path bypass the cents conversion and pass semitones, matching the voice's existing math).
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/reverb.js` L53** — At decay=10 (documented max) the comb feedback is exactly 1.0, so the reverb never decays and accumulates ongoing input until it clips.
  - Fix: Compute per-comb feedback from loop time instead of a fixed map: fb_c = Math.pow(10, -3 * (combLen_c / sampleRate) / decay), clamped ≤0.98. This keeps loop gain <1 at all settings and makes every comb decay at the same rate.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/sidechain.js` L38** — Sidechain ducks on every 16th step regardless of the trigger pattern, because drum patterns are arrays of {velocity,accent} objects and `if (voiceSteps[i])` treats every step object (even velocity:0) as a hit — so the advertised kick-pump never happens and the target just gets near-constant attenuation.
  - Fix: In getTriggerPositions, resolve object-format steps: `const isHit = (v) => v && (typeof v !== 'object' ? (v !== 0) : v.velocity > 0);` then `if (isHit(voiceSteps[i])) hitSteps.push(i)`. Since session.jb01Pattern/jt90Pattern are always full object arrays at render time, the numeric index-array branch is dead in practice and the ambiguous `v===0||v===1` gate detection can be dropped for the object path.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L363** — Track volume, mute, solo, pan, and track inserts (RoutingManager state mutated by set_track_volume/mute_track/solo_track/add_insert) are never read by the renderer, so those tools report success while the rendered audio is unchanged.
  - Fix: In the mix loop, resolve each instrument buffer's track (match track.nodeId to buffer id), skip if muted or if any solo exists elsewhere, multiply by 10^(track.volume/20), apply constant-power pan, and run track.inserts through the existing EFFECT_PROCESSORS before summing. Until implemented, make the routing tools return an explicit 'not applied at render yet' error instead of success.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jbs-node.js` L128** — JBSNode stores producer units while every other instrument node and both tool write paths assume engine units, so every jbs slot-param write is double-converted at render (R11, R2).
  - Fix: Make JBSNode store engine units like all other nodes: in _registerParams convert defaults via toEngine (as jb01 does), delete the toEngine calls in getEngineParam/getSlotEngineParams (return stored value), and drop the producer-range clamp in setParam (lines 102-111). Update serialize()'s default-comparison to compare engine defaults (as jt90-node.js:315 does).
- **[dsp-other] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L118** — Generic tweak/tweak_multi double-convert every JB-S slot parameter because they convert producer→engine before session.set, but JBSNode stores producer units and converts again at render — so all jbs values reach the audio ~100x (or dB-scale) wrong, while get_param round-trips cleanly and hides it.
  - Fix: Make JBSNode follow the engine-unit storage convention like every other instrument node: in _registerParams set `this._params[path] = toEngine(paramDef.default, paramDef)`, delete the toEngine calls in getSlotEngineParams/getEngineParam (return stored values directly), and fix show_jbs (jbs-tools.js:197) to display via fromEngine. Then delete the now-wrong engine-unit writes in tweak_jbs or leave them (they become correct).
- **[dsp-other] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L153** — tweak_multi writes engine-converted values into effect nodes that store producer units (render reads them raw), and get_param applies fromEngine to those producer values — so the generic write path silently makes effect params ~100x too small and the generic read path reports them 100x too large, while tweak_effect writes raw producer values to the same node.
  - Fix: Standardize one storage convention for EffectNode (engine, matching instrument nodes): convert in EffectNode.setParam via toEngine using the registered descriptor and convert back in getParams for render (or teach the effect DSP to take engine units). Then generic tweak/tweak_multi/get_param work unchanged and tweak_effect must route through the same toEngine bridge (currently mixer-tools.js:438 `effectObj._node.setParam(key, value)` with no conversion).
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L153** — Effect nodes store producer units while instrument nodes store engine units, so the generic read/write paths double-convert and silently corrupt every non-choice fx param (breaks R11's single-bridge rule and R7's one-storage-convention).
  - Fix: Pick one storage convention. Cheapest: mark effect descriptors `producerStored: true` (or detect nodes under 'fx.') and skip toEngine/fromEngine for them in get_param/tweak/tweak_multi — effect DSP already consumes producer units. Cleaner long-term: store engine units in effect nodes like instruments and convert in the processor functions.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/sidechain.js` L39** — Sidechain ducks on EVERY step, not on trigger hits: JB01 patterns are arrays of {velocity, accent} objects, and the gate-array branch treats every object (including velocity:0) as a hit.
  - Fix: Handle the object format explicitly: `const hit = typeof v === 'object' ? (v?.velocity > 0) : !!v;` — or better, per the next finding, stop parsing instrument-specific formats inside the effect and pass resolved hit positions in.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L419** — runAgentLoop's while(true) only handles stop_reason end_turn and tool_use; any other stop reason (max_tokens — likely with max_tokens: 1024 — or refusal) falls through both ifs and re-sends the identical request forever: an unbounded API-billing loop with no iteration cap and no error surface.
  - Fix: Add a terminal else: append response.content, surface `callbacks.onResponse` with a truncation/refusal note, and break. Raise max_tokens (e.g. 8192) and add a max-iterations guard (e.g. 30) as a backstop.
- **[model] `jambot/jambot.js` L424** — The only live model call site, the main producer agent loop (runAgentLoop), pins the retired model claude-sonnet-4-20250514, so every jam request now fails with a 404.
  - Fix: Replace line 424 with `model: "claude-fable-5",` — the loop is pure creative/music-production judgement, which per the owner's direction leans Fable. The call sends no `thinking` or sampling params, so the swap is clean (Fable runs always-on adaptive thinking when `thinking` is omitted; temperature/top_p are absent, so no 400s). If per-turn cost matters for trivial tweaks ("the hats are too loud"), `claude-opus-5` is the sanctioned cheaper alternative for the same single call site (Fable 5 is $10/$50 per MTok; Opus 5 shipped 2026-07-24, after the cached pricing table). Note Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention on the org and can return stop_reason "refusal" (see the loop-handling finding).

### Major (81)

- **[dsp-screech] `web/public/jt30/dist/machines/jt30/engine.js` L233** — At high resonance + high envMod the modulated cutoff parks at the 5500Hz hard cap on every note onset and the ladder self-oscillates at a fixed ~3796Hz whistle (with drive harmonics at 7.6/11.4/15.2kHz), violating the stated regression criterion (no narrow line >25dB prominence above 2.5kHz at >-40dBFS).
  - Fix: Make the feedback damping bite at the engine's own cap, not at Nyquist: in moog-ladder.js scale damping by (fc/0.25)^2 (or equivalently ensure r stays below ~2.8 for cutoff <= 5.5kHz at res 100), and/or in engine.js make the env approach the cap asymptotically instead of clamping (e.g. soft-knee on octaves), and/or make the cap track the knob (min(5500, baseCutoff*2^3.5)) so accent-onset timbre follows the cutoff knob again instead of ringing at one fixed pitch.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L423** — tweak_jt30's schema documents level as 'Output level 0-100' but the implementation treats it as mixer gain in dB clamped to [-60,+6], so any docs-following value (7-100) slams +6dB and hard-clips the output, and the documented range is 94% dead.
  - Fix: Change the tweak_jt30 schema text to 'Output level in dB (-60 to +6)' to match the automate tool's wording, or convert 0-100 producer units to dB in jt-tools.js before session.set (e.g. dB = (level-80)/80*60 style mapping); same audit should be run on the sibling tweak_jt10/jb202 schemas.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb202/dist/machines/jb202/engine.js` L188** — Slide/portamento is effectively instantaneous (~0.5 ms), so the slide step flag produces no audible glide — its only audible effect is skipping the envelope retrigger; the slideDuration=0.05 field is dead code.
  - Fix: Use slideProgress as the actual interpolator: currentFreq = startFreq * (targetFreq/startFreq)^easedProgress over slideDuration (exponential-in-pitch glide over the full 50 ms), and delete the 0.1 one-pole; or set the one-pole coefficient from slideDuration (k = 1 - exp(-1/(slideDuration*sampleRate/4.6)) ≈ 0.002).
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jt10/dist/machines/jt10/engine.js` L205** — glideTime has zero audible effect (every slide completes in under 20 ms), and glideTime=0 leaves slid notes stuck at a wrong pitch between the two notes.
  - Fix: Derive the per-sample smoothing from slideDuration: k = 1 - Math.exp(-1/(max(slideDuration,0.001)*sampleRate)) and use currentFreq += (targetFreq-currentFreq)*k (or glide linearly in semitones over slideProgress); snap currentFreq=targetFreq when slideDuration<=0 or when slideProgress reaches 1.
- **[docs-drift] `web/public/jt10/dist/machines/jt10/engine.js` L230** — subMode behavior contradicts both the tool docs and the engine's own header: 0 is documented as 'off' but plays a -1 oct sub, 1 is documented as '-1 oct' but plays -2 oct, and 2 ('-1 oct pulse' per the header) is identical to 1.
  - Fix: Pick one contract and align all three surfaces: either implement 0=off (skip sub when subMode===0), 1=-1oct, 2=-2oct in processSample, or fix the tool description and jt10-params.json hint to '0=-1oct, 1/2=-2oct' and delete the '-1 oct pulse' claim from the engine header.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L371** — tweak_jt10's schema tells the producer filterCutoff is 0-100, but the handler converts it as Hz (20-16000), so a doc-following producer asking for a fully-open filter (100) gets a nearly-closed 100 Hz filter.
  - Fix: Change the tool description to 'Filter cutoff in Hz (20-16000)' and amend the UNITS sentence in the tweak_jt10 description; no handler change needed.
- **[architecture] `web/public/jt10/dist/machines/jt10/engine.js` L266** — JT10 still carries the additive-Hz envelope mapping the jt30 fix removed (base + envMod*env*8000, clamp 16000), patched over by the envResCap hack that silently throws away up to 55% of the resonance knob at high envMod instead of fixing the mapping.
  - Fix: Port the jt30 cure: map filter env exponentially in octaves above baseCutoff with an absolute cap (~5.5 kHz for sweeps), delete envResCap, and rely on cutoff-frequency-dependent resonance damping in the ladder for the top of the range — restores full resonance for acid patches and closes the envMod=0 screech path in one move.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/engine.js` L146** — renderPattern renders exactly stepDuration*totalSteps with zero tail, so any voice still ringing at the last bar boundary is hard-cut to silence in one sample, producing an audible pop at the end of every render — while the session mixer reserves +2 s 'Extra time for release tails' that JB01 leaves silent.
  - Fix: In JB01Engine.renderPattern, extend the offline render length past the last step (e.g. duration = stepDuration*totalSteps + 2, matching core/render.js line 255) while keeping event scheduling unchanged; the mixer already accommodates the longer buffer.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/voices/snare.js` L18** — The snare 'decay' parameter (documented 0-100, 'length') does nothing: this.decay is stored and clamped but never read in trigger(), whose envelope times are all hard-coded.
  - Fix: Scale the three envelope times by decay in trigger(), e.g. const d = 0.5 + this.decay; osc1 ramp 0.15*d, osc2 0.08*d, noiseDecay = (0.15 + this.snappy*0.1)*d, and stop times to match.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/voices/cymbal.js` L96** — Units mismatch: the node sends decay as engine-normalized 0-1 but CymbalVoice interprets it as seconds clamped 0.3-4, so the producer's 0-100 knob only spans ~0.26-0.9 s of ring, the designed default (1.5 s) and top range (4 s) are unreachable, and the knob's upper half is audibly dead.
  - Fix: Map engine 0-1 onto the voice's real range in setParameter (cymbal: decay = 0.3 + value*3.7; hihat: decay = 0.02 + value*1.98), or convert in jb01-params.json/converters with a seconds unit for these voices.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/tools/jt-tools.js` L303** — tweak_jt90 `level` is documented as 'Volume 0-100' but the value is fed to toEngine with the dB paramDef (-60..+6), so 6..100 all clamp to +6dB, level=0 is a no-op at default volume, and the voice can never be attenuated with documented values.
  - Fix: In jt-tools.js tweak_jt90, map the 0-100 producer value to dB before toEngine (e.g. 0→-60dB, 80→0dB, 100→+6dB, or value→20*log10(v/80)), or change tool-definitions.js:467 to document dB (-60..+6) like tweak_jb202 does.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/tools/jt-tools.js` L311** — tweak_jt90 `tune` is documented as cents ±1200 but the value goes through the semitones paramDef (clamp ±12, then ×100), so any cents value is amplified 100× and anything beyond ±12 saturates to a full ±1 octave.
  - Fix: Either divide input.tune by 100 (cents→semitones) before toEngine in jt-tools.js:309-314, or change tool-definitions.js:461/468 to 'tune in semitones (-12 to +12)' to match params/jt90-params.json.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jt90/dist/machines/jt90/engine.js` L486** — The mix-bus 'soft limiter' fastTanh(sample*0.7)/fastTanh(0.7) has an asymptotic ceiling of 1.655 (not 1.0), so stacked voices at DEFAULT levels overshoot 1.0 and hard-clip (flat-top) in the final WAV.
  - Fix: Make the limiter ceiling ≤1: use sample = fastTanh(sample) (unity slope and ceiling 1.0) at engine.js lines 360, 486, 510, or multiply the current expression by fastTanh(0.7); alternatively clamp/normalize in core/render.js before WAV write.
- **[model] `jambot/params/jt90-params.json` L54** — Default tom tuning is inverted: hitom default tune -12st puts the HIGH tom at 80Hz, below the MID tom's 90Hz, and lowtom's -12st default lands at sub-bass 40Hz — a default tom fill goes 40→90→80Hz instead of ascending.
  - Fix: Change hitom.tune default from -12 to ~0..-2 (≈140-160Hz) and lowtom.tune default from -12 to ~0..-2 (≈70-80Hz) in jt90-params.json (lines 44/54), keeping midtom -5, so defaults ascend low<mid<hi.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jp9000/dist/modules/filter-biquad.js` L28** — filter-biquad allows Q up to 30 with no gain compensation, clipping the output at any q >= ~5.
  - Fix: Compensate output gain by ~1/Q above Q~1 (or cap q at ~10 and soft-clip), mirroring whatever compensation lands in the lp24 fix.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jp9000/dist/rack.js` L236** — Two connections into the same input port silently replace instead of summing — the earlier source vanishes from the mix.
  - Fix: In the input-wiring loop, accumulate: allocate a mix buffer when a port has >1 incoming connection and add each source into it (or reject the second connect with an error telling the user to use the mixer module).
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jp9000/dist/rack.js` L60** — A feedback connection is accepted without error but makes the entire patch render pure silence, reported as success.
  - Fix: Either detect cycles in connect() and reject with an error, or support them properly with one-block-delayed feedback (persist output buffers across process() calls instead of nulling inputs).
- **[code-quality] `jambot/tools/jp9000-tools.js` L165** — tweak_module (and remove_module, disconnect_modules, pluck_string) report success for nonexistent modules and misspelled params, so patch edits silently do nothing.
  - Fix: Have rack.setParam/module.setParam return false or throw on unknown module/param, and make each tool return an Error string listing valid modules/params (matching connect_modules' existing behavior).
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/tools/jp9000-tools.js` L150** — set_jp9000_output accepts a nonexistent module and the subsequent render is a fully silent WAV delivered with a success message.
  - Fix: Validate module and port existence in setOutput (throw like connect does); optionally warn at render time when the output module is missing.
- **[architecture] `web/public/jp9000/dist/rack.js` L26** — Auto-generated module IDs use modules.size+1, so after any removal a new addModule can reuse an existing ID and silently replace that module.
  - Fix: Use a per-rack monotonic counter (this._nextId++) or loop until an unused ID is found; also make addModule throw if an explicit id already exists.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/tools/jp9000-tools.js` L198** — Pattern step velocity is documented as 0-1 but never clamped, and values >1 multiply straight through env/VCA into heavy clipping.
  - Fix: Clamp velocity to [0,1] in add_jp9000_pattern normalization (and in JP9000Node.renderPattern / EnvADSRModule.trigger as defense).
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tools/jp9000-tools.js` L197** — The pattern 'accent' field is documented as 'Accent for dynamics' and stored, but has zero effect on the audio.
  - Fix: Apply accent in renderPattern (e.g. velocity boost x1.3 capped at 1, like the 303-style instruments) or remove accent from the tool schema and description.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/instruments/jp9000-node.js` L293** — JP9000 silently ignores session swing, drifting against every other instrument in a swung session.
  - Fix: Offset gated steps by swing*maxSwingDelay on odd 16ths in renderPattern, same formula as jbs-node.js:296-305.
- **[dsp-other] `instruments/jbs-node.js` L241** — Multi-bar JB-S patterns are silently truncated to 16 steps unless slot s1 happens to be programmed, because renderPattern takes patternLength from pattern.s1 only (empty s1 -> length 0 -> falls back to 16), dropping every hit at step >= 16.
  - Fix: patternLength = Math.max(16, ...SLOTS.map(s => pattern[s]?.length || 0)) so the longest programmed slot defines the loop length.
- **[dsp-other] `instruments/jbs-node.js` L260** — The JB-S node output level is applied twice — once as renderPattern's masterGain (getOutputGain) and again at mixdown in core/render.js (instData[i] * level) — so any node-level setting acts at double strength in dB.
  - Fix: Apply node output gain in exactly one place: set renderPattern's masterGain to 1.0 (unity) and let the render.js mixdown apply getOutputGain(), matching whichever convention the other instrument nodes use.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/delay.js` L309** — The in-loop soft saturator has small-signal gain of 1+3*amount^2 (up to 4x = +12 dB), so effective loop gain is feedback*(1+3a^2) and the delay self-oscillates into a permanent loud drone at feedback settings far below 100.
  - Fix: Normalize the saturator to unity small-signal gain before mixing, e.g. const shaped = (driven / (1 + Math.abs(driven))) / drive; return x * (1 - amount) + shaped * amount * drive... simplest correct form: return x*(1-amount) + (driven/(1+Math.abs(driven)))*(amount/drive)*... — concretely: replace the mix line with `return x * (1 - amount) + (driven / (1 + Math.abs(driven))) * (amount / drive);` so d/dx at 0 == 1 for all amounts; the tanh-style limiting of large peaks is preserved.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/delay.js` L199** — In pingpong mode the feedback parameter is silently multiplied by spread (crossGain = spread/100 in both cross-feed terms), so at spread=0 feedback does nothing at all — any feedback value yields exactly one repeat — and low spread values shorten the tail, contradicting the param docs ('spread: Stereo width (pingpong mode only)').
  - Fix: Decouple width from regeneration: keep total feedback gain constant and use spread only to steer where it goes, e.g. `toDelayL = input + (feedbackR * cross + feedbackL * (1 - cross)) * feedbackGain; toDelayR = (feedbackL * cross + feedbackR * (1 - cross)) * feedbackGain;` with cross = spreadAmount — spread=0 then degenerates to two parallel mono delays with full feedback, spread=100 stays true ping-pong.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L172** — The reverb tail is hard-truncated to digital zero at the exact end of the pattern — the effect chain processes the instrument's bar-length buffer, while the +2s release pad exists only in the master context.
  - Fix: Zero-pad the instrument buffer by the tail allowance (e.g. +2s, or decay-dependent) before processEffectChain so reverb/delay tails ring into the pad instead of being chopped at the bar boundary.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/reverb.js` L53** — The decay parameter (unit 'seconds') is wildly inaccurate and additionally controlled by size: 0.1–2s of range produces almost no change, and RT60 varies 6x with size at fixed decay.
  - Fix: Same fix as the feedback=1.0 finding: derive fb per comb from decay and that comb's actual loop time (fb = 10^(−3·loopSec/decay)), which makes 'seconds' accurate and size-independent by construction.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/reverb.js` L55** — damping=100 (documented '100=dark') silences the reverb tail entirely instead of darkening it — damp2=0 zeroes the feedback path.
  - Fix: Scale like stock Freeverb: `const damp = (damping / 100) * 0.4;` (Jezar's scaledamp), keeping the loop lowpass from ever fully opening the feedback kill; 100 then reads as maximally dark rather than off.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/filter.js` L31** — Linear resonance->Q mapping (0-100 -> Q 0.5-20) is far too hot with no gain compensation: the DEFAULT resonance 30 adds a +16 dB peak at cutoff, so a plain 'lowpass the drums' request clips the master, and resonance 100 applies +26 dB.
  - Fix: Make the mapping perceptual and the default tame: e.g. q = 0.5 + Math.pow(resonance/100, 2) * 19.5 (res 30 -> Q ~2.3/+7 dB) and/or apply makeup attenuation 1/max(1,Q*0.5) after filtering; keep default resonance <= 10 so mode+cutoff-only usage stays near Butterworth.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L326** — Automation stored under alias paths (drums.*, bass.*, lead.*, synth.*) is accepted by session.automate() but silently dropped at render, because the harvest loop matches canonical instrument prefixes only.
  - Fix: Canonicalize at store time: in ParamSystem.automate(), use _resolveNode(path) and re-key the automation entry as `${canonicalId}.${paramPath}` (build an alias→canonical map at registration, or compare node identity). Alternatively, harvest in render by resolving each automation path with _resolveNode and comparing the resolved node to the rendering node.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L268** — The renderer hardcodes its own canonical instrument list — including phantom id 'jb200' which no longer exists — instead of iterating the registry, and it disagrees with session.getCanonicalInstruments(), which itself omits jp9000; three hand-maintained lists have already drifted.
  - Fix: Make one source: derive the instrument list from the ParamSystem registry (iterate session.params.nodes, dedupe by node identity to skip aliases, filter `typeof node.renderPattern === 'function'`), implement getCanonicalInstruments() on top of that, and have render.js call it. Delete 'jb200' from the list and unregister jb200-tools (or delete the file).
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L154** — session._nodes is a second, parallel node registry duplicating every ParamSystem.register() call, and core render.js reads it (`session._nodes[id]`, render.js:274) — bypassing the registry the docs call the single path; a node registered in only one of the two maps is invisible to the other consumer.
  - Fix: Delete _nodes; give ParamSystem a `getNode(id)` accessor and have render.js and the allowlisted tools use it (or session.getCanonicalInstruments() once it's registry-backed). Extend test-platform-rules.js to scan core/ as well.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/core/automation.js` L4** — The automation service claims to work on ANY parameter path, but fx.* and master.* automation is accepted by automate() and then never applied: render.js only forwards instrument-prefixed automation into renderPattern(), and effect params are read once per render (effect._node.getParams(), render.js:65), never per step; the three application helpers in this file are exported and dead.
  - Fix: Either apply effect automation in processEffectChain (chunk the buffer per step, call getAutomationAt(path, step) and set params before each chunk), or make automate() reject non-instrument paths with a clear error and fix the docstring. Delete applyAutomationAtStep/getAutomationValuesAtStep/interpolateAutomation or wire them into the render path.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L550** — serializeSession() never serializes session.routing, so save/load silently loses all tracks, sends, and send routing; RoutingManager.serialize()/deserialize() (routing.js:251, 290) exist but have no callers.
  - Fix: Add `routing: session.routing ? session.routing.serialize() : undefined` to serializeSession, and in deserializeSession/restoreSessionInPlace reconstruct via `new RoutingManager()` + deserialize(data.routing) when present.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/routing.js` L67** — Send and track parameters live entirely outside the ParamSystem — createSend never registers the effect node, so no fx.* path reaches a send's params and generic tweak/get_param cannot see them — and each send/insert carries a stale `params` snapshot alongside the live node, two sources of truth that already disagree at serialize time.
  - Fix: Pass the ParamSystem (or session) into RoutingManager; in addSend register the effect node as e.g. `fx.send.{id}` and unregister in removeSend. Delete the `params` snapshot fields from createSend/addTrackInsert; serialize from `effectNode.getParams()` instead.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L88** — The PRIMARY generic tweak tool rejects every fx.* path — the exact effect addressing the contract documents — because it validates only the first path segment as a node id, defeating core _resolveNode's multi-segment resolution; tweak_multi lacks the check and works, so the two primary write tools disagree.
  - Fix: Replace the first-segment check with resolution: expose `session.params.resolve(path)` (wrapping _resolveNode) and error only when it returns null — same one code path get/set already use.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jb01-node.js` L130** — The single write path has no unit contract, so the node guesses units by magnitude and auto-converts — a second, heuristic conversion path beside converters.js that misclassifies legitimate small producer values and makes read/write asymmetric (set 55, read 0.55).
  - Fix: Pick one convention for node.setParam (engine units), do all producer→engine conversion in exactly one place (the tool boundary plus one conversion step where render consumes automation), and delete the magnitude heuristics from instrument nodes — fail loudly on out-of-range instead of guessing.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/routing.js` L43** — The effect type→node-class dispatch is maintained in five places with inconsistent coverage and a silent fallback: routing.js createSend defaults unknown effect types to Delay instead of erroring, addTrackInsert supports only 3 of 5 types, addMasterInsert only 2, and the EFFECT_NODE_CLASSES map is copy-pasted between session.js and mixer-tools.js despite a comment claiming it is shared.
  - Fix: Move EFFECT_NODE_CLASSES into effects/index.js (or core), import it in session.js, mixer-tools.js, and routing.js; replace all three switches with a lookup that throws on unknown type; let sends/inserts accept every registered effect type.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L384** — createSession contains ~240 lines of hand-written per-instrument accessors (drumParams/bassParams/jt10Params/jt30Params/jt90Params/jbsParams proxies plus pattern getters, level wiring, serialize fields), forming a second public param-write API beside session.set and forcing 6+ session.js edit sites per new instrument; jbsParams even hardcodes its param list instead of reading descriptors.
  - Fix: Define one INSTRUMENTS table [{id, aliases, NodeClass}] and loop it for construction, registration, levels, patterns/currentPattern, and serialization. Keep the memo-sanctioned pattern accessors as a generated map (session.pattern('jt90') or generated getters), and deprecate/delete the per-instrument *Params proxies in favor of session.set/get.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L102** — Effect chains are stored under whatever target string the agent typed (mixer-tools uses the raw channel key) but rendered only under canonical-id keys, so an insert added with the documented alias vocabulary ('drums.kick', 'bass') is silently never rendered — the same canonicalization gap as automation.
  - Fix: Canonicalize the target once at add_effect/add_channel_insert time (resolve the instrument segment through the ParamSystem alias map before keying effectChains and registering fx.* paths), mirroring how patterns are canonical-only.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/jb200-tools.js` L28** — The jb200 node was removed from session registration but its tools are still loaded (tools/index.js:44): add_jb200 reports success while producing no audio, and save_pattern('jb200')/show('jb200') crash (R4, R18, R20).
