- **[dsp-other] `jambot/instruments/jbs-node.js` L260** — JBSNode applies its own output gain inside renderPattern while render.js applies node.getOutputGain() again at mix time, so the jbs level is applied twice — a bespoke path no other node has (R5, R3).
  - Fix: Delete the getOutputGain() application inside JBSNode.renderPattern (set masterGain.gain.value = 1.0 or connect voices straight to destination); render.js already owns node-level gain.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jb01-node.js` L341** — renderVoices() in JB01 and JT90 ignores options.automation, so adding any voice-level effect silently disables all parameter automation for that instrument (R3, R9).
  - Fix: Destructure automation in both renderVoices implementations and pass the per-voice slice of engineAutomation to each solo engine.renderPattern call, reusing the conversion block already present in renderPattern.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L325** — Automation stored under an alias path ('drums.kick.decay') is accepted but silently dropped at render, because render.js collects only canonical-ID prefixes (R16, R2).
  - Fix: Normalize to canonical ID at store time in ParamSystem.automate(): resolve the node, look up its canonical id (first registration), and store the automation path with the canonical prefix — mirroring 'patterns stored by canonical ID only'.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jt90-node.js` L448** — JT90 keeps node-local _swing (second source of timing truth beside the Clock) and a _accentLevel knob that is never passed to the engine — a settable parameter that does nothing (R12).
  - Fix: Delete _swing/_accentLevel plus their accessors and session.jt90Swing/jt90AccentLevel proxies; renderPattern uses options.swing (from clock) only. If accent level is wanted, register it as a real descriptor param and forward it to the engine.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/instruments/jb200-node.js` L11** — The jb200 stack (node, engine, params JSON, tool wiring) is dead but still shipped in 12 files, so a parallel legacy bass synth keeps drifting against jb202 (R13, R5); removal breaks these files.
  - Fix: One removal commit: delete jb200-node.js, jb200-tools.js, params/jb200-params.json, web/public/jb200/; strip the references above (converters.js registry entry, build.js copy list, render canonicalIds, song/session/midi branches, index.js exports); run node tests/run-tests.js.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L528** — The canonical instrument list is hand-duplicated in at least four places and they disagree, instead of services iterating the node registry (R3, R5).
  - Fix: Make session.getCanonicalInstruments() the single source (derived from a CANONICAL_IDS const next to node construction, including jp9000), have render.js and song-tools iterate it, and generate the save_pattern enum from it.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L87** — Generic tweak rejects every fx.* path — the canonical addressing example in the contract — because its bespoke validation checks only the first path segment against the node map, while ParamSystem resolves multi-segment IDs like 'fx.jb01.delay1' via progressive prefixes (R2, R10: add_effect registration is supposed to 'make tweak() work for free').
  - Fix: Drop the first-segment check; validate by attempting resolution instead — e.g. `if (session.getDescriptor(path) === undefined && session.get(path) === undefined) return error`, or expose a public `session.resolves(path)` that wraps ParamSystem._resolveNode, and rely on session.set's boolean return for the failure message.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L467** — tweak_jt90's schema lies about both level and tune units: it says 'level 0-100' and 'tune in cents (-1200 to +1200)' but jt90-params.json defines level as dB (-60..+6) and tune as semitones (-12..+12), so an agent following the schema slams levels to +6dB and pins tunes to the clamp rail.
  - Fix: Rewrite the schema descriptions to match the params JSON: level 'Volume in dB (-60 to +6, 0=unity)', tune 'Pitch in semitones (-12 to +12)', mute 'sets level to -60dB' — same wording tweak_jb01 already uses. Also expose kick 'sweep' (defined in jt90-params.json, reachable only via generic tweak today).
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L423** — tweak_jt30's schema says 'Output level 0-100' and mute 'sets level to 0' but the handler writes the value straight to the node's dB level, so level:80 becomes a +80dB request (clamped to +6dB max boost) instead of 80%.
  - Fix: Fix the schema to 'Output level in dB (-60 to +6, 0=unity)' and mute to 'sets level to -60dB', matching tweak_jt10/tweak_jb202 which document the identical handler behavior correctly.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L371** — tweak_jt10's schema says 'filterCutoff 0-100' but the parameter is Hz (20-16000, log): an agent sending a knob value like 50 gets a 50Hz nearly-closed filter, while Jambot's own CLAUDE.md example passes Hz (2000).
  - Fix: Change the schema description to 'Filter cutoff in Hz (20-16000)' like tweak_jt30/tweak_jb202. Same file also under-documents filterEnvAmount as plain 0-100 — verify each jt10 property against jt10-params.json while touching it.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L886** — save_preset/load_preset/list_presets are advertised in the agent schema but have no registered handler — preset-tools.js is never imported by initializeTools — so every call returns 'Unknown tool'; and the orphaned implementation wouldn't work anyway (its instrument list disagrees with the schema enum and it reads pre-node legacy session fields).
  - Fix: Either remove the three entries from TOOLS, or rewrite preset-tools.js generically (serialize node params via node.getParams()/serialize() per R9, instrument list = session.listNodes()), align its instrument names with the schema enum, and add it to initializeTools.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/jb200-tools.js` L39** — The whole JB200 tool family is a dead limb wired three inconsistent ways: its 6 tools are registered but absent from the agent schema, the JB200 node is never registered in the session, tweak_jb200 crashes with a TypeError, add_jb200 reports success while writing an orphan property nothing ever renders, and the still-exposed show tool crashes when asked for jb202 because its alias maps to the missing jb200 node.
  - Fix: Delete jb200-tools.js (moving test_tone, which IS in the schema, into analyze-tools.js or its own file), remove the jb200/jb202→showJB200 mapping in session-tools.js show (point jb202 at a JB202 show fn or generic get_state), and drop the jb200 branches in song-tools.js and create_session's orphan session.jb200Params/jb200Pattern writes (session-tools.js:295-319).
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/song-tools.js` L100** — save_pattern/load_pattern are ~270 lines of ten copy-pasted per-instrument branches doing the identical snapshot (pattern+params+automation+inserts) — exactly the bespoke per-component code R3/R5 forbid — and the drums/bass/lead/jb200 branches throw TypeErrors because session.patterns never contains those keys, while jp9000 (which IS in session.patterns) has no branch at all.
  - Fix: Replace both with one generic implementation: resolve alias→canonical via the existing node alias map, then `session.patterns[id][name] = { pattern: node.getPattern(), params: node.getParams(), automation: getAutomationForInstrument(session, id), channelInserts: getInsertsForInstrument(session, id) }` and the symmetric restore via setPattern/setParam — the InstrumentNode interface already guarantees every method needed. Delete the dead drums/bass/lead/jb200 branches.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/mixer-tools.js` L307** — Effect chains keep a params snapshot beside the live node (a second source of truth): show_effects/show_mixer display the snapshot, render reads the node, and only tweak_effect updates both — so any generic-path write leaves the display lying (R2: one way to read).
  - Fix: Remove the params snapshot from chain entries ({id, type, _node} only) and make show_effects/show_mixer/serialization read `e._node.getParams()` (formatting through fromEngine/formatValue once units are unified).
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/mixer-tools.js` L36** — add_channel_insert/add_master_insert duplicate add_effect almost line-for-line (two ways to append an effect to the same effectChains, with divergent replace-vs-append semantics), and their schemas lie: add_channel_insert advertises a 'ducker' effect that guarantees an error, add_master_insert's enum allows only 'eq' though the handler accepts five types, and the channel enum omits every JT-series target though the handler takes any.
  - Fix: Make add_channel_insert/add_master_insert thin wrappers over the add_effect implementation (or delete them from TOOLS and keep add_effect as the one path), replace 'ducker' with 'sidechain' in the enums, widen add_master_insert's enum to the real EFFECT_NODE_CLASSES keys, and drop the target enum in favor of a free-form target validated against registered nodes.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L87** — The PRIMARY generic tweak tool cannot write ANY effect parameter — it errors on every fx.* path, so the documented 'fx.master.delay1.feedback' write path (R2, R4) does not exist.
  - Fix: Replace the first-segment check with the resolver the rest of the system uses: `if (!session.getDescriptor(path) && session.params._resolveNode(path) === null) return error`. ParamSystem._resolveNode already handles multi-segment IDs; tweak just never calls it.
- **[architecture] `jambot/effects/sidechain.js` L108** — The sidechain effect hardcodes specific instruments and receives the entire session via renderContext, violating R3 (services know signals/parameters, never instruments) — and the leak causes wrong ducking in arrangement mode.
  - Fix: Resolve trigger positions in render.js from the same pattern object being rendered (iterate session.getCanonicalInstruments(), ask each node for hit steps of the trigger voice via an interface method), and pass `{ triggerPositions }` to processSidechain instead of `{ session }`. Derive the trigger choice list from registered instrument voices.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L52** — Each chain effect keeps TWO param stores (`params` snapshot + `_node`) that drift: writes through the canonical session.set path are lost on save/load, and shown stale by show_effects.
  - Fix: Make `_node` the only store: serializeEffectChains should read `e._node ? e._node.getParams() : e.params`; drop the snapshot from chain entries (or refresh it in one place) and delete the backwards-compat branch in applyEffect.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/mixer-tools.js` L281** — Effect chains are keyed by the raw target string while the render loop only looks up canonical instrument IDs, so add_effect on an alias ('bass', 'drums') reports success but the effect never renders (R16: canonical-ID-only storage).
  - Fix: Normalize the target to its canonical ID in add_effect/add_sidechain/add_channel_insert before keying the chain: resolve via the registered node (`session.params.nodes.get(target)`) and map node→canonical id, mirroring how patterns are stored canonical-only.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/routing.js` L43** — The effect-type→class mapping exists in at least five places that already disagree, so adding an effect is not the documented 'one-liner' and the copies have drifted (R5/R7).
  - Fix: One EFFECT_REGISTRY module exporting {type: {NodeClass, processor}}; session.js, mixer-tools.js, routing.js and render.js import it; derive tool-schema enums from Object.keys(registry).
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L610** — The effect tool schemas advertise capabilities the handlers reject and hide ones they support — including a 'ducker' effect type that always errors.
  - Fix: Map 'ducker'→'sidechain' in the handler (routing.js:89 already does this) or fix the enum; generate all three enums from the shared effect registry so they cannot drift.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/mixer-tools.js` L440** — tweak_effect is a second, non-deprecated way to write effect params that disagrees with the generic path on units — two ways to write, different stored values (R2).
  - Fix: After fixing the generic tools' fx handling, delete tweak_effect (and its schema) or reduce it to a thin wrapper that builds fx paths and calls the same conversion code as tweak.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L543** — session.routing (send buses, track→send routings, track config) is silently dropped by save/load — serializeSession never includes it (breaks R20 save()/load() and R19's send architecture).
  - Fix: Add `routing: session.routing?.serialize()` to serializeSession and `if (data.routing) { session.routing = new RoutingManager(); session.routing.deserialize(data.routing); }` to deserializeSession and restoreSessionInPlace.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/routing.js` L59** — add_send silently drops all effect params, and an unknown effect type silently becomes a DelayNode that still carries the bogus type label and is then skipped entirely at render — triple silent failure violating the repo's fail-loudly rule (R5).
  - Fix: In createSend: throw on unknown type, and apply params via `for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(params)) node.setParam(k,v)` exactly like add_effect does. Standardize all five node constructors to NOT interpret config as params (delete SidechainNode's special-casing) so there is one way to initialize an effect.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/routing.js` L66** — Send effect nodes are never registered in ParamSystem (their params are unreachable by any read/write path — R2 'if a value exists, the agent can see it'), and track volume/mute/pan are never read by the renderer, making set_track_volume and mute_track silent no-ops.
  - Fix: Register send nodes as `fx.send.{id}` on addSend (unregister on removeSend); apply `track.volume`/`mute` as a gain factor in the send-accumulation loop and the main mix, or delete set_track_volume/mute_track until they do something.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tools/index.js` L44** — JB200 is half-removed: its node is no longer registered in session.js, yet six jb200 agent tools remain registered and reachable via the headless API (R20), where add_jb200 reports success while silently producing nothing and every other jb200 tool crashes — violating R1 (clean add/remove), R4/R18 (tool claims done without effect), R8 (tools reach into session._nodes), and R16 (patterns table has no jb200 key).
  - Fix: Delete the jb200 surface completely: remove `await import('./jb200-tools.js')` from tools/index.js:44, delete tools/jb200-tools.js, remove the jb200 branches in tools/song-tools.js (lines 165-172, 304-312, 397, 463, 485) and showJB200 in tools/session-tools.js (lines 13, 74-135, 341), remove 'jb200' from render.js:268 canonicalIds, delete instruments/jb200-node.js + its export in instruments/index.js:13, remove JB200_PARAMS from params/converters.js:28,38, drop 'jb200-params.json' from build.js:41, and delete params/jb200-params.json + presets/jb200/. Then run node jambot/tests/run-tests.js (R6).
- **[dsp-screech] `jambot/tests/run-tests.js` L12** — The mandatory suite contains zero rendered-audio regression tests, so the JT30/JT10 resonance screech (shipped for ~1 month, fixed in commit 7db5075fd 2026-02-22 'tame resonance screech on JT30 + JT10 when envelope mod is active') could not have been caught, and its regression still can't be.
  - Fix: Missing test #1 (highest value): per-instrument render-and-analyze smoke test in run-tests.js — for each canonical instrument via createHeadless(), load a stress pattern (for JT30/JT10: resonance ~90 + filterEnvAmount ~80, the exact screech trigger), render 2 bars, then run the in-repo SpectralAnalyzer.detectResonance() and assert no peak above 2kHz with prominenceDb > 30 and high-band(2-10kHz)/full-band RMS ratio under a threshold. All pieces (headless.js, SpectralAnalyzer, AnalyzeNode) already exist in-repo — test-analyze.js proves the analyzer works; it's just never pointed at Jambot's own renders. Missing test #2: determinism check (R14) — render the same session twice, byte-compare the WAVs. Also add test-jb01-jt10-combo.mjs to the runner.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tests/test-platform-rules.js` L46** — No test in the suite ever calls session.get()/session.set() — the system's single documented read/write API (R2) — and no test touches any fx.* path, so effect-parameter addressability (R10's 'This makes tweak() work for free') and alias resolution (R16, 'drums.kick.decay') are entirely untested.
  - Fix: Missing test #3: full addressability sweep — create a session, add every effect type (delay, eq, filter, sidechain, reverb) on master and on one instrument chain via the add_effect tool, enumerate every path registered in ParamSystem, and for each path assert session.get(path) returns a value, session.set(path, midpoint) round-trips through session.get, and a descriptor exists. Include alias paths (drums.*, bass.*) asserting they resolve to the canonical node. This single test closes R2, R10-registration, and R16 at once.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tests/test-param-roundtrip.js` L17** — Both param tests hardcode a 6-entry ALL_PARAMS list, silently excluding jb200-params.json and sampler-params.json (both loaded by converters.js), which breaks PLATFORM.md's 'Zero test code to write for basic coverage' promise — a new instrument's params JSON gets no coverage unless someone remembers to edit two test files.
  - Fix: Replace both hardcoded maps with a glob: `readdirSync('../params').filter(f => f.endsWith('-params.json'))`, keyed by filename prefix. Any new params JSON then gets roundtrip + consistency coverage automatically, matching the documented promise. Add jb200 to CANONICAL_IDS or delete the dead jb200 node/params/tools.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/tests/test-param-roundtrip.js` L50** — Unit-conversion tests assert only invertibility (fromEngine(toEngine(x)) ≈ x), which any matched wrong pair of curves satisfies — a broken dB taper, Hz log curve, or pan law would pass every one of the 371 assertions; the suite pins exactly one absolute value (JT90 tune 500 cents).
  - Fix: Missing test #4: golden conversion table — a literal table of (unit, def, producerValue, expectedEngineValue) rows: dB {max:6}: 6→1.0, 0→0.5012, -60→~0.0005; '0-100': 50→0.5; pan: -100→-1, 100→1; Hz {min:20,max:20000}: 632.46→0.5; semitones: 5→500; bipolar {-50..50}: 0→0.5. Assert toEngine to 1e-3 and fromEngine inverse. This locks the curves themselves, which round-trip structurally cannot.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tests/test-defaults-consistency.js` L11** — The web-vs-headless parity check (R7/R13) covers only JT90, and the test header explicitly codifies the drift it exists to prevent: every other instrument keeps private parallel defaults in its web engine, untested.
  - Fix: Extend Part 2 to every instrument with a web engine: import each engine's DEFAULT_PARAMS/param-defs and diff against the params JSON, failing on new private defaults. Longer term (missing test #5, parity): since offline nodes already import the same engine.js from web/public (e.g. jt10-node.js:287), render a fixed pattern through the node and through the engine driven directly, and RMS/byte-compare — proves ONE SYNTH holds in audio, not just in defaults.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/ui.tsx` L906** — setSession({ ...session }) after every agent turn degrades the session facade: spreading the session converts its accessor proxies (jb202Pattern etc.) into dead data properties, so from the second prompt on, tool pattern writes never reach the instrument nodes and renders silently ignore them.
  - Fix: Never spread the session. Keep it in a useRef (stable identity) and force re-renders with a separate counter: `const [rev, setRev] = useState(0); ... setRev(r => r+1)`. Replace all three `setSession({ ...session })` sites.
- **[model] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L424** — The model is hardcoded to claude-sonnet-4-20250514 — a deprecated model (Anthropic migration guide lists its retirement as June 15, 2026, now past) — with no env var or ~/.jambot config override, so every Jambot user is pinned to a model that may already 404.
  - Fix: Read `JAMBOT_MODEL` from the same env-file chain getApiKey() uses, defaulting to a current model (claude-opus-4-8): `model: process.env.JAMBOT_MODEL || 'claude-opus-4-8'`. Document it in CLAUDE.md next to the API-key section.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/midi.js` L426** — JB200→JB202 rename drift silently kills bass export twice over: hasContent() returns key `hasJB200` while project.js destructures `hasJB202` (always undefined), and midi.js reads `session.jb200Pattern`, a proxy that no longer exists on the unified session — so /export omits jb202-bass.mid and the README says '(not used)' even with a programmed bass line, and generateFullMidi writes an empty JB202 track.
  - Fix: In midi.js rename hasJB200→hasJB202 and read `session.jb202Pattern` (also in generateFullMidi and generateJB202Midi); grep consumers for the old key. Add a tiny test that programs one bass note and asserts hasContent(session).hasJB202 === true.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/ui.tsx` L676** — /status crashes: it reads session.pattern and session.voiceParams, legacy fields that do not exist on the unified node-based session, so Object.keys(undefined) throws and the exception escapes handleSubmit's try (which only wraps runAgentLoop).
  - Fix: Rebuild /status on the public session API (session.jb01Pattern / jb202Pattern / etc., or reuse buildMixOverview) and delete the pattern/voiceParams fields from project.js createProject.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L354** — R3/R5 violation with behavioral impact: buildSessionContext hardcodes three instruments (JB01/JB202/Sampler), so JT10/JT30/JT90/JP9000 state is invisible in the agent's CURRENT SESSION STATE between turns — the model literally cannot see an acid line it programmed on the previous prompt; buildMixOverview (/mix) and ui.tsx StatusBar have the same bespoke three-instrument lists.
  - Fix: Add one generic session-level service (e.g. session.getActiveInstruments() iterating registered nodes via getDescriptor()/getPattern()) and have buildSessionContext, buildMixOverview, StatusBar, and midi.hasContent all consume it — the current four divergent copies are what produced the hasJB202 bug.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L220** — R8 violation: buildMixOverview reaches past the public API into session._nodes (jb01 at :220, jb202 at :252) and imports per-instrument param tables (JB01_PARAMS/JB202_PARAMS) directly, exactly the pattern PLATFORM.md forbids ('never session._nodes... this keeps instruments swappable').
  - Fix: Expose a public non-default-params query on session (e.g. session.getNonDefaultParams(instrumentId) built on ParamSystem definitions, returning producer-unit values) and rewrite buildMixOverview generically over all registered instruments.
- **[model] `jambot/jambot.js` L419** — The while(true) loop handles only stop_reason end_turn and tool_use; any other stop_reason (max_tokens, or Fable 5's refusal) matches neither branch and the identical request is re-sent forever — an infinite API-billing loop.
  - Fix: After the tool_use branch add: `else { messages.push({ role: "assistant", content: response.content }); callbacks.onResponse?.(response.stop_reason === "refusal" ? "Request declined by safety classifiers." : "(response truncated — hit token limit)"); callbacks.onEnd?.(); break; }` — i.e., terminate the loop on any non-tool_use stop reason.

### Minor (69)

- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L150** — add_jb202's description (and the jb202-node.js header, line 6) says the synth uses a '24dB cascaded biquad filter', but the engine instantiates MoogLadderFilter — a completely different topology with 303-style resonance behavior.
  - Fix: Update both descriptions to 'Moog ladder filter (24dB/oct, 303-style resonance)'.
- **[code-quality] `web/public/jb202/dist/machines/jb202/engine.js` L221** — processSample calls filter.setCutoff(modCutoff) every sample, which recomputes all ladder coefficients 44,100x/s even when the cutoff is unchanged (e.g. envelope idle), bypassing the >1 Hz change-guard that moog-ladder.js already implements in processWithMod.
  - Fix: In processSample, only call setCutoff when |modCutoff - filter.getCutoff()| > 1 Hz (mirror the processWithMod guard).
- **[code-quality] `jambot/tools/jt-tools.js` L114** — tweak_jt10 silently ignores lfoWaveform — the param is defined in jt10-params.json (choice: triangle/square/sh) and used by the engine, but is missing from both the tool schema and the handler's paramMap.
  - Fix: Add lfoWaveform to the tweak_jt10 input schema (enum: triangle/square/sh) and to the paramMap in jt-tools.js (choice unit passes through toEngine untouched).
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/engine.js` L243** — The advertised hi-hat choke ('ch cuts oh', engine header) is a no-op in all offline renders — the choke branch only contains a comment — so the open-hat tail rings through closed-hat hits; audible impact is small because the oh envelope is already quiet by the time ch lands.
  - Fix: In schedulePatternInContext, track the last oh trigger's masterGain and, when a ch event lands at time t, schedule gain.cancelScheduledValues(t); setValueAtTime(current,t); exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, t+0.02) on that gain (offline contexts accept scheduled automation; the 'can't choke' assumption is wrong — only currentTime-based choke() is unavailable).
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jb01/dist/machines/jb01/voices/hihat.js` L44** — Hats are 13-15 dB quieter than kick/snare at equal level settings and cannot reach kit-competitive level even at the +6 dB maximum, forcing producers to duck everything else instead.
  - Fix: Raise the hat/cymbal internal make-up gain (e.g. masterGain = level*1.0 for hats, oscillatorGain ~0.25) or rebalance kit defaults so 0 dB settings produce comparable peaks; verify against 909 reference balance.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jt90/dist/machines/jt90/voices/kick.js` L173** — KickVoice hard-deactivates at exactly 2s regardless of remaining envelope, producing an audible tick at the end of long-decay kick tails.
  - Fix: Replace the hard cutoff with a short fade (e.g. multiply envFast/envSlow by 0.995/sample once past 2s) or raise the amp threshold so the cut lands below -60dB.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/tools/jt-tools.js` L309** — tweak_jt90 silently accepts and confirms parameters a voice does not have (e.g. clap tune), reporting success while doing nothing.
  - Fix: When getParamDef returns null, respond 'clap has no tune' instead of setting a dead path; drop the /100 and raw fallbacks. Same applies to kick.sweep, which exists in jt90-params.json but is absent from the tweak_jt90 schema/handler (reachable only via automate).
- **[docs-drift] `web/public/jt90/dist/machines/jt90/voices/sample-voice.js` L208** — Tone comment claims 'tone=0 → dark (LP cutoff ~2kHz)' but lpCoeff=0.05 is a one-pole at ~360Hz, so tone=0 near-mutes the hats and acts as a large uncompensated volume cut.
  - Fix: Either fix the comment, or map tone to an actual cutoff (e.g. lpCoeff = 1-exp(-2π·fc/sr) with fc = 2k..bypass) and add gain compensation at low tone.
- **[architecture] `web/public/jt90/dist/machines/jt90/voices/hihat.js` L164** — voices/hihat.js (the Chamberlin-SVF 6-oscillator hat) and voices/cymbal.js are dead code — engine.js imports SampleVoice for ch/oh/crash/ride, so the f=1.2 SVF clamp is unreachable from any producer-facing path; the SVF is stable anyway.
  - Fix: Delete or archive voices/hihat.js and voices/cymbal.js (or wire them up as an optional synth-hat mode); no DSP change needed for stability.
- **[dsp-other] `web/public/jp9000/dist/modules/string.js` L41** — Karplus-Strong delay length is rounded to whole samples with no fractional-delay correction, detuning notes by up to ~6.5 cents.
  - Fix: Add a first-order allpass fractional-delay stage in the loop tuned to the rounding remainder, or at least document the tuning limit above ~C4.
- **[dsp-other] `sample-voice.js` L107** — Slot level is applied twice inside SampleVoice (envGain peak = velocity*level AND gainNode = level*2.0), leaving a hidden -6 dB at the documented '0 dB unity' default and a dB-squared level curve once the conversion bug is fixed.
  - Fix: Use level only in the static gainNode (level*2.0) and make the per-trigger envelope peak just `velocity` (peakLevel = velocity), keeping velocity scaling linear as measured.
- **[code-quality] `instruments/jbs-node.js` L175** — JBSNode.trigger() is dead code: it validates the kit/slot and computes `const params = this.getSlotEngineParams(slot);` then returns without ever creating a voice or playing anything.
  - Fix: Either implement it (create/reuse a SampleVoice and call voice.trigger(time, velocity)) or delete the method so callers fail loudly instead of silently.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/reverb.js` L59** — The wet/dry mix is a linear crossfade (dry = 1 − wet), giving a −6dB dip in the dry signal at mix=50 instead of an equal-power blend.
  - Fix: Equal-power law: dryGain = Math.cos(wetGain * Math.PI/2), wet scaled by Math.sin(wetGain * Math.PI/2) (or sqrt crossfade), so mid-mix settings don't duck the source.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/reverb.js` L12** — Late tail shows mild metallic modal flutter inherent to the 8-comb Freeverb topology — isolated spectral lines exceed the 20dB-prominence threshold at damping=0, though at low absolute level.
  - Fix: Structural quality note (Schroeder/Freeverb: 8 parallel combs → 4 series allpasses, mono-summed input, +23-sample R offset). If it ever matters: add slight per-comb modulation (0.1–0.3 samples LFO on comb read position) or more comb lines to break up the surviving high-Q modes; keeping damping ≥20 in presets already masks it.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/effects/eq.js` L116** — EQ is CLEAN — all band gains match claimed dB within 0.06 dB (no defect; recorded here as the verification result, not a bug).
  - Fix: No fix needed.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/core/node.js` L372** — Dead parallel abstractions are exported as public API: MixerNode (a third mixer-state model beside session.mixer and RoutingManager, which would have made tracks.*.volume addressable) and the ParamSystem singleton getParamSystem/resetParamSystem (a second way to obtain a ParamSystem beside per-session construction) have zero callers.
  - Fix: Delete MixerNode, getParamSystem, and resetParamSystem (and their index.js exports); if track params should become addressable, do it by registering RoutingManager in the ParamSystem rather than reviving MixerNode.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/core/session.js` L490** — session.mixer's shape is defined in three places with three different shapes, and mixer.masterVolume is a dead knob — initialized to 0.8 in all three, settable by nothing, and never applied at render (render.js's masterGain 0.8 is connected to a source-less OfflineAudioContext, so it renders silence and does nothing).
  - Fix: Export one createMixerState() from core and use it in all three sites; either apply masterVolume as a final buffer multiply in renderSession or delete the field; delete the pointless masterGain/silent-base-render block (allocate the output Float32Arrays directly).
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/render.js` L253** — render.js hardcodes 16 steps per bar one line after querying the Clock for the rest of its timing, bypassing clock.stepsPerBar and breaking silently if beatsPerBar/stepsPerBeat are ever changed.
  - Fix: Replace with `const stepsPerBar = session.clock.stepsPerBar;`.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/session.js` L484** — JT90 keeps a private second swing source with tangled precedence against the master Clock: session.jt90Swing writes jt90Node._swing, and at render the node uses `swing || this._swing`, so the instrument swing only applies when clock swing is exactly 0 — two timing authorities where R12 mandates one.
  - Fix: If per-instrument shuffle is a wanted feature, model it as an offset the node adds to clock swing (documented, addressable as a normal param jt90.swing via descriptors); otherwise delete jt90Swing and _swing and use the clock exclusively.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/core/session.js` L93** — Two competing default BPMs: Clock declares DEFAULT_BPM = 120, but createSession and restoreSessionInPlace both override with `|| 128`, so the clock's own default is unreachable and a falsy stored bpm restores to a different tempo than a fresh clock.
  - Fix: Pass config.bpm through undefined (`bpm: config.bpm`) and let Clock's `?? Clock.DEFAULT_BPM` be the single default; set DEFAULT_BPM to 128 if that is the intended house default.
- **[dsp-other] `jambot/core/automation.js` L130** — generateAutomation's 'random' pattern uses unseeded Math.random(), so regenerating the same automation request is non-reproducible; values are baked into the stored array so a given render stays deterministic, keeping this a nit rather than a trigger-path violation of R14.
  - Fix: Use the project's seeded PRNG (accept an optional seed argument defaulting to a fixed constant) so identical calls produce identical curves.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/index.js` L24** — The instruments barrel cannot be imported at all — it re-exports three node files that no longer exist — and it still exports the dead JB200Node (R15, R6).
  - Fix: Rewrite index.js to export only the nodes that exist (JB01, JB202, JBS, JT10, JT30, JT90, JP9000) or delete it; add a trivial import-smoke test to tests/run-tests.js so a broken barrel fails CI.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jp9000-node.js` L300** — JP9000Node.renderPattern ignores the options.pattern/options.params/options.swing overrides that the renderPattern contract (and every other node) honors (R1, R9).
  - Fix: Destructure 'pattern = this._pattern' from options like jb202-node.js:257 does, and apply a params override when provided (map onto rack.setParam); document swing as unsupported or apply it in the step loop.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jp9000-node.js` L52** — JP9000 module parameters are writable via setParam but invisible to the descriptor system, so list_params/get_state/getDescriptor cannot see them and unit conversion never applies (R2, R7).
  - Fix: Have addModule() register each module's param descriptors into _descriptors (rack modules already know their param ranges) and unregister on removeModule; or generate descriptors dynamically in getParameterDescriptors() from rack.modules.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jb01-node.js` L118** — 'mute' is a write-only phantom parameter with three different bespoke implementations across nodes, and unmuting is impossible — mute=false is silently swallowed and the pre-mute level is destroyed (R2, R1, R5).
  - Fix: Register 'mute' as a real boolean descriptor on the base InstrumentNode, store it as state (getParam returns it), stash the prior level on mute and restore on unmute, and let render multiply gain by !mute — one implementation in core/node.js, delete all three per-node branches.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/instruments/sampler-node.js` L300** — sampler-node.js is an orphaned near-verbatim duplicate of jbs-node.js that has already drifted — it hardcodes 16-step looping where jbs supports variable pattern length (R5, R17).
  - Fix: Delete instruments/sampler-node.js; the 'sampler' legacy alias already resolves to JBSNode via params.register('sampler', jbsNode) (session.js:123).
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jb01-node.js` L130** — JB01 setParam heuristically sniffs producer-vs-engine units and silently converts, creating a second accepted write dialect that no other node has and that masks caller unit bugs (R2, R11).
  - Fix: Delete the sniffing block — keep the warn if desired but do not convert; the deserialize() migration path (lines 419-441) already covers legacy saved data, which is the only legitimate producer-unit source.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/instruments/jb01-node.js` L330** — Five nodes carry a _getAutomationForRender()/_renderAutomation back-channel whose comment claims render.js populates it, but nothing anywhere writes _renderAutomation — dead vestigial path (R9).
  - Fix: Delete _getAutomationForRender() from all five nodes and the 'automation || this._getAutomationForRender()' fallbacks; renderPattern takes automation solely from options.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/instruments/jb202-node.js` L91** — JB202 (and JB200) getParam docblocks claim producer-friendly units but the stored/returned values are engine units (R11 documentation drift).
  - Fix: Fix the docblocks to say ENGINE UNITS (0-1), matching jb01-node.js:90's correct wording.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jbs-node.js` L199** — Per-voice pattern access has three bespoke shapes: JBS overloads the standard getPattern/setPattern signature with a slot argument, JB01 uses get/setVoicePattern, JT90 uses get/setTrackPattern+setTrackStep (R1, R5).
  - Fix: Standardize on one optional per-voice accessor pair on InstrumentNode (e.g. getVoicePattern/setVoicePattern) and make JBS's getPattern/setPattern signature match the base exactly; migrate jt90's Track* names.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/instruments/jbs-node.js` L191** — JBSNode.trigger() computes slot params and discards them (dead stub), and the '-6dB default for proper gain staging' in JB01/JBS constructors is dead because createSession immediately overrides level to 0 (R17 dead code / docs drift).
  - Fix: Delete the trigger() stubs (renderPattern is the real path; base class already throws for unimplemented trigger), and either honor -6 dB in createSession ('config.jb01Level ?? -6') or drop the misleading constructor default+comment.
- **[architecture] `jambot/instruments/jb202-node.js` L229** — render.js passes options.swing to every node but JB202/JT30/JT10/JP9000 silently ignore it, so clock swing shuffles drums while melodic lines stay straight with no error or documentation (R9, R12).
  - Fix: Either forward swing into the melodic engines' step scheduling (they receive stepDuration already) or document/strip it: have render.js not pass swing to nodes whose descriptor declares no swing support, so the contract is explicit rather than silently divergent.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/session-tools.js` L76** — Multiple tools reach past the public session API into underscore internals (session._nodes, node._params, node._voices) in direct violation of the R8 memo, and jp9000-tools even constructs a node straight into session._nodes without ParamSystem registration, which would leave a replacement node unaddressable.
  - Fix: Add the missing public accessors to session.js (session.hasNode(id) already effectively exists via listNodes(); pattern writes should go through the session.jb202Pattern/jb01Pattern setters which already call setPattern) and route ensureJP9000 through a session.ensureNode(id) that registers in ParamSystem. Then delete every `_nodes`/`_params`/`_voices` reference in tools/.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/sampler-tools.js` L1** — sampler-tools.js (378 lines) is dead: never imported by initializeTools, none of its tools (list_kits, load_kit, add_samples, ...) are registered or in the schema, and it is a near-verbatim fork of jbs-tools.js that also hard-codes engine-unit defaults contradicting the params JSON (R7).
  - Fix: Delete tools/sampler-tools.js (the 'sampler' alias already resolves to the jbs node, and jbs-tools covers every operation).
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L4** — The schema header claims 'all 65 tools' while the array holds 97 (with 101 handlers registered), and none of the per-instrument tweak_* entries carry the deprecation the contract declares — the agent-facing descriptions are richer than generic tweak's, actively steering the agent toward the deprecated path (R4).
  - Fix: Drop the count from the header comment; prefix each deprecated tool's schema description with 'DEPRECATED — prefer the generic tweak() with a path' (or remove them from TOOLS once the generic-path unit bugs above are fixed).
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/song-tools.js` L436** — set_arrangement stores sections under legacy alias keys (drums/bass/lead) that the renderer's canonical-ID loop never reads, so an alias-keyed section silently renders silence — R16 requires resolving aliases to canonical IDs at storage time.
  - Fix: In set_arrangement map incoming alias keys to canonical IDs (drums→jb01, bass→jb202, lead→jt10 per the session alias registry) before storing, and drop the alias keys from the stored object.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/automation-tools.js` L32** — The automate handler supports pattern/min/max/steps generation that the schema never documents, making that whole code path unreachable by the agent.
  - Fix: Either add pattern/min/max/steps to the automate schema (documented in producer units) or delete the generation branch and generateAutomation import.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L1263** — route.level and add_sidechain.amount take raw 0-1 engine units at the agent boundary while every other mix parameter is producer-unit (0-100/dB), breaking the R11 rule that engine units stay inside; add_sidechain also hides its attack/release/hold params from the schema.
  - Fix: Accept 0-100 in the schema for route.level and sidechain.amount, divide by 100 in the handlers, and add attack/release/hold (ms, documented) to add_sidechain's schema.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/generic-tools.js` L256** — get_state prints raw stored engine values while get_param prints producer units for the same parameters — two read paths with different unit presentations (R2/R11), inviting the agent to feed an engine value (0.5) back into tweak as a producer value.
  - Fix: In get_state, look up each descriptor (already iterating session.describe(node)) and render with the same fromEngine+formatValue pipeline get_param uses.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/jt-tools.js` L31** — stepsToPattern is copy-pasted verbatim between jt-tools.js and jb01-tools.js, and add_jt90 (jt-tools.js:223-276) is a near-verbatim clone of add_jb01 — per-instrument duplication of what should be one shared helper (R5).
  - Fix: Extract stepsToPattern and a generic addDrumPattern(session, patternProp, voices, input) into a shared tools/pattern-helpers.js and have both add_jb01 and add_jt90 delegate to it.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/effects/delay-node.js` L24** — Two competing choice-descriptor conventions across effect nodes: delay uses `choices:` with numeric values, filter/sidechain use `options:` with string values — and the generic layer only understands `options`, so delay's choice labels are invisible and unvalidated.
  - Fix: Standardize on `options:` with string values (matching converters.js validate() which reads `options`); store the string, translate in the processor; add choice validation to Node.setParam using converters.validate.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/effects/delay-node.js` L41** — DelayNode.getSyncedTime() and getMode() have zero callers, and processDelay re-implements the identical sync table with drifted semantics (string-tolerant where the node method is numeric-only) — duplicated logic the contract (R7) forbids.
  - Fix: Delete getSyncedTime/getMode from DelayNode, or have processDelay call node-level helpers via params — one sync table, one owner.
- **[architecture] `jambot/effects/sidechain-node.js` L21** — Effect descriptors use units outside the contract's six types ('ms', 'seconds', 'Q', '0-1', 'bpm', 'boolean'); worst is sidechain amount exposed as 0-1 at the agent boundary while every comparable knob in the system is 0-100 (R11).
  - Fix: Change amount to 0-100 (divide by 100 in processSidechain); either add 'ms'/'s' to the official converter vocabulary as explicit pass-through units or fold time params into the six types — but declare it in converters.js, not implicitly via the default branch.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/effects/analyze-node.js` L32** — AnalyzeNode is a 1013-line file (2.5x the 400-line review gate, R17) that extends Node rather than EffectNode while living in effects/, and its tool-side singleton is never registered in ParamSystem — pseudo-params (including a bpm that shadows the Clock, R12) that no generic tool can see.
  - Fix: Move it out of effects/ (services/ or analysis/), split into stats/waveform/sidechain-detect modules under 400 lines each, and drop the registerParams pretence — pass bpm as a function argument.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/core/node.js` L372** — MixerNode (105 lines with its own tracks/sends/master param routing) is exported but never instantiated anywhere — a third parallel representation of mixer state alongside session.mixer.effectChains and RoutingManager.
  - Fix: Delete MixerNode (and its core/index.js export). If mixer params should be addressable later, register RoutingManager-backed nodes in ParamSystem instead of keeping a dead alternative.
- **[architecture] `jambot/tests/test-interface-contract.js` L89** — No test exercises the fx.* read/write round trip, so every critical breakage above passes the mandated architecture test suite (R6): effects have no params JSON, which silently exempts them from the automatic consistency/round-trip coverage instruments get.
  - Fix: Add tests/test-effect-roundtrip.js: for each type in the effect registry, add_effect → tweak every param via generic tools → assert node value and get_param display → serialize/deserialize → assert values survive. Run it from run-tests.js.
- **[architecture] `jambot/sample-voice.js` L13** — JB-S breaks the ONE-SYNTH rule (R13): jambot's local SampleVoice/KitLoader (used for offline render) and web/public/jbs/dist/sampler/'s SampleVoice/KitLoader (used by the web UI) are two divergent implementations of the same sampler — 239 and 236 diff lines respectively — with incompatible level semantics, so web playback and Node render of the same kit cannot match; CLAUDE.md's carve-out ('except JB-S which is local') documents only the jambot copy and hides that a second, drifted web engine exists.
  - Fix: Pick one engine: move the current jambot SampleVoice/KitLoader into web/public/jbs/dist/sampler/ (replacing the stale compiled copies) and change jambot/instruments/jbs-node.js:10 to import from '../../web/public/jbs/dist/sampler/sample-voice.js' like every other instrument; update the web JBS UI to the unified level semantics; delete jambot/sample-voice.js + kit-loader.js and the CLAUDE.md:290-295 carve-out.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/CLAUDE.md` L567** — CLAUDE.md's own new-synth checklist instructs duplicating the core engine ('copy from existing synth'), directly contradicting its 'Do NOT duplicate synth code' rule (R13/R5) — and the codebase already holds five copies of core/engine.js (jb01, jbs, 909, 90s byte-identical; jb200 drifted), the exact mechanism that produced the original jb200 drift problem.
  - Fix: Create one canonical shared core (e.g. web/public/synth-core/ or fold into web/public/jb202/dist/core/), have each machine's engine.js import SynthEngine from it via relative path (same pattern as the shared jb202 DSP imports used by JT10/JT30/JT90/JP9000), delete the per-synth core/ copies, and change CLAUDE.md:567 from 'copy from existing synth' to 'import from the shared core — never copy'.
- **[docs-drift] `web/public/jb200/dist/sequences.json` L38** — The legacy jb200 data and UI drifted from jb202 after the handoff and both remain live: jb200's sequences carry a different note than jb202's 'ONE SYNTH' fix (G1 vs G2), jb200's presets lack the 'Drift' preset, the Next.js route web/app/jb200/page.tsx still serves the old WebAudio synth, and jambot's preset loader (presets/loader.js:38) will happily serve jb200 kits/sequences for an instrument that can no longer render — three competing preset sources (web/public/jb200/dist, web/public/jb202/dist, jambot/presets/jb200/) for one bass synth.
  - Fix: Archive web/public/jb200 and web/app/jb200 (or delete — jb202's README already documents jb200's Web-Audio inconsistency as the reason it was replaced), and delete jambot/presets/jb200/. If the web page must stay for history, add a deprecation banner and exclude jb200 from jambot's preset loader search.
- **[docs-drift] `web/public/jbs/dist/core/voice.js.map` L1** — For the jambot-era synths (jb01, jb202, jt10, jt30, jt90, jp9000, jbs) the dist/ folders ARE hand-edited source with no build script, but that is only documented for the old machines (synthmachine/README.md covers 909/90s/303/101/mixer only), and jbs/909/90s dists still ship orphaned .d.ts and .js.map files whose sourceRoots point at TypeScript that no longer exists — inviting an editor to assume a build step and edit the wrong layer.
  - Fix: Add one line to jambot/CLAUDE.md 'Synth Sources': 'These dist/ folders are hand-edited JavaScript source — there is no build step; edit them directly.' Delete the orphaned *.d.ts and *.js.map files from web/public/{jbs,909,90s}/dist/.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/dist/params/converters.js` L34** — jambot/dist/ is a committed esbuild output (last built Jan 31) that has drifted ~5 weeks behind live source — its converters.js predates the JBS rename and the 'SINGLE CONVERSION PATH' guarantee — leaving a second, stale, greppable copy of every engine/param module inside the working tree (unlike releases/v0.1.0, which is properly frozen and imported by nothing).
  - Fix: Add jambot/dist/ to .gitignore and remove it from the index (build.js regenerates it on demand); keep releases/vX.Y.Z/ as the only committed frozen artifacts, per RELEASE-ENGINEERING.md.
- **[architecture] `jambot/core/automation.js` L131** — core/automation.js has zero test coverage (R11's 'values stored in producer units, converted to engine units at render time' is unverified for every instrument), and it calls Math.random() in value generation — an R14 violation that no platform-rule pattern check guards against despite test-platform-rules.js's own charter.
  - Fix: Missing test #5a: automation round-trip — set automation on one param per unit type in producer units via the tool layer, render, assert the engine values applied at each step match toEngine(expected) (each instrument node does the conversion, so run it for every canonical instrument). #5b: add a Math.random pattern rule to test-platform-rules.js scanning instruments/, core/, effects/, and web/public/*/dist/dsp/, with a seeded-PRNG allowlist; fix automation.js:131 to use a seeded PRNG stored in the session.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/tests/test-interface-contract.js` L126** — The negative EffectNode test is vacuous: it is named 'EffectNode with missing methods throws on validateInterface' but asserts doesNotThrow on a broken effect, verifying nothing.
  - Fix: Define `class BrokenEffect extends EffectNode { }` then `Object.defineProperty(BrokenEffect.prototype, 'getParams', { value: undefined })` (or subclass with `getParams = undefined` as an own field) and `assert.throws(() => new BrokenEffect().validateInterface(), /missing required methods/)`, mirroring the working InstrumentNode negative test at lines 80-87.
- **[code-quality] `jambot/tests/test-interface-contract.js` L40** — The interface-contract test itself reaches past the public API with session._nodes (R8), because session exposes no public node enumerator — the same gap the platform-rules tech-debt comment already names.
  - Fix: Add `session.listNodes()` / `session.getNode(id)` to core/session.js, use it in the test and in automation-tools.js, and shrink the _nodes allowlist accordingly.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/PLATFORM.md` L19** — PLATFORM.md's testing instructions are stale: it says three test files when the runner has six, and claims the round-trip test discovers params via converters.js when it actually hardcodes its own list.
  - Fix: Update PLATFORM.md:18-19 to say 'all six test files' (or better, 'the full suite') and remove the converters.js discovery claim — or make it true by implementing the glob fix from the ALL_PARAMS finding.
- **[docs-drift] `jambot/tests/test-defaults-consistency.js` L37** — The test whitelists a 'bipolar' unit that the contract's exhaustive six-unit list (dB, 0-100, semitones, Hz, pan, choice) does not define, so test and docs disagree on the unit-type surface (R11).
  - Fix: Add 'bipolar' to the documented unit list in PLATFORM.md and CLAUDE.md (it has a well-defined converter: linear, center→0.5) and add it to the golden conversion table test; alternatively migrate bipolar params to semitones/0-100 if six units is a hard design constraint.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/midi.js` L365** — R8 violation with zero-cost fix: generateFullMidi and hasContent read `session._nodes?.jt90?.getPattern?.()` (and jt30/jt10) even though the public proxies session.jt90Pattern / jt30Pattern / jt10Pattern already exist for exactly this.
  - Fix: Replace each `session._nodes?.X?.getPattern?.()` with `session.XPattern || {}` (or `[]`).
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/tools/tool-definitions.js` L266** — R2/R4 drift: the deprecated per-instrument tweak_* tools (tweak_jb01, tweak_jb202, tweak_jbs, tweak_jt10, tweak_jt30, tweak_jt90) are still shipped to the model alongside the PRIMARY generic tweak, with no deprecation note in their schemas — the agent sees seven ways to write one parameter while CLAUDE.md promises one.
  - Fix: Either drop the tweak_* entries from TOOLS (keep handlers registered for headless back-compat) or prefix their descriptions with 'DEPRECATED — use tweak with a path instead' so the model routes to the generic tool.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L305** — The LEVELS section of buildMixOverview is dead: it reads session.jb01Level / jb202Level / samplerLevel, proxies that don't exist on the unified session, so /mix can never display instrument levels even when they're set.
  - Fix: Add public level getters to session.js (get jb01Level() { return jb01Node.getLevel(); } etc., matching the pattern proxies) and iterate all registered instruments, not three.
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L455** — Tool-name string special-casing inside the generic agent loop ('render' and 'test_tone' get renderPath) is bespoke per-tool code (R5) and is inconsistent with headless.js, which special-cases only 'render' — test_tone via headless writes to cwd instead of the project path.
  - Fix: Move path resolution into render-tools.js: always pass a `getRenderPath` callback in context and let the tools that need a path call it; delete both call-site name checks.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L422** — Cache-hostile prompt construction: the system prompt is rebuilt every loop iteration with volatile session state appended, and 97 tool schemas are re-sent at full input price on every tool round-trip — no cache_control anywhere, so nothing is ever served from prompt cache.
  - Fix: Keep system static (JAMBOT_PROMPT + genreContext) with `cache_control: {type:'ephemeral'}` on it, and inject the volatile CURRENT SESSION STATE as a text block in the latest user turn instead.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L485** — R17 violation: jambot.js is 885 lines against the repo's own <400-line code-review gate — the agent loop shares a file with API-key management, mix-overview rendering, and ~400 lines of static guide/help/splash text (SPLASH, HELP_TEXT, CHANGELOG_TEXT, seven instrument guides); ui.tsx is 978 lines.
  - Fix: Extract the static text to guides.js (pure data), buildMixOverview/buildSessionContext to core or a status.js, and api-key handling to config.js — jambot.js keeps only the agent loop (~150 lines).
- **[architecture] `vibeceo/jambot/project.js` L239** — R8 rule breach (works today via the legacy alias): updateSession reaches into session._nodes.sampler.serialize() for the kit ID instead of asking a public API — and the adjacent comment admits the data is already in the serialized output it just stored.
  - Fix: Read it from the value already computed: `project.session.samplerKitId = serialized.params?.nodes?.jbs?.kitId ?? null;` (restoreSession already falls back to `saved.params?.nodes?.sampler?.kitId`).
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/midi.js` L282** — Dead code: generateDrumsMidi, generateBassMidi, and generateLeadMidi are exported but imported nowhere, and the legacy alias generateJB200Midi is exported twice (midi.js:432 and re-exported project.js:301) with zero consumers; generateLeadMidi additionally reads session.leadPattern, which has no session proxy.
  - Fix: Delete the three unused generators and both alias exports.
- **[code-quality] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L15** — Dead import: listProjects is imported from project.js but never referenced in jambot.js (the /projects flow lives in ui.tsx, which imports it itself).
  - Fix: Delete the import line.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/jambot.js` L27** — Stale comment: the TOOLS import is annotated '65 tools for Anthropic API' but TOOLS.length is 97.
  - Fix: Drop the count from the comment ('Tool definitions for the Anthropic API') so it can't drift again.
- **[docs-drift] `vibeceo/jambot/ui.tsx` L732** — /analyze is described as 'Analyze last render (levels, frequencies, recommendations)' but the handler only prints the static ANALYZE_GUIDE help text — it never runs an analysis.
  - Fix: Either run the analyze_render tool against the last render path and print the result, or change the description to 'Audio analysis guide'.
- **[model] `jambot/dist/jambot.js` L18162** — The esbuild bundle in dist/ has the retired model id baked in and must be regenerated after the source fix — not hand-edited.
  - Fix: After editing jambot.js, rerun the build (`node build.js`) so dist/jambot.js picks up `claude-fable-5`. Leave releases/ frozen as instructed.
- **[model] `jambot/package.json` L12** — @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.71.2 (installed exactly 0.71.2) is compatible with the new ids — model strings are passed through untyped and the call uses only model/max_tokens/system/tools/messages — but is old enough to lack typed support for newer params.
  - Fix: No change required for the model swap. Optionally bump @anthropic-ai/sdk to latest in both package.json:12 and build.js:66 (keep them in sync) if you later want typed output_config.effort or the refusal-fallback middleware for Fable 5.

## Documentation drift (from the contract pass)

- Stale aliases in PLATFORM.md and STATUS.md: both alias tables say bass/lead/synth → jb200, but code (core/session.js:131-133) registers them to jb202, and TOOLING-STATUS.md marks JB200 'deprecated — do not use'. PLATFORM.md Part 2 also still teaches the agent 'bass / lead / synth (JB200)' with add_bass/add_lead examples and calls it a 'Polysynth' while CLAUDE.md calls JB202 a monosynth.
- JAMBOT-PROMPT.md (the agent system prompt) contradicts the architecture contract and current tool surface: it instructs use of per-instrument tweak_jb01/tweak_jb200 (CLAUDE.md says per-instrument tweak_* tools are DEPRECATED, tweak is primary); uses path 'jb200.bass.<param>' (CLAUDE.md says 'jb202.{param}'); references tools create_send/route_to_send (CLAUDE.md/PLATFORM.md name them add_send/route); names the sampler 'sampler' with add_samples/tweak_samples (canonical ID is 'jbs'); its instruments table omits JT10/JT30/JT90 entirely.
- Tool-count drift across three docs vs code: STATUS.md says 65 tools, CLAUDE.md headless section says 'All 91 tools', RELEASE-NOTES says '65+' — actual TOOLS array today has 97.
- Sampler and JT-line naming is inconsistent across docs: JB-S/jbs (CLAUDE.md, PLATFORM.md) vs 'sampler' (STATUS.md canonical list, JAMBOT-PROMPT.md) vs R9DS (RELEASE-NOTES, docs/FREE-SAMPLES.md, UI-MIGRATION-PLAN status bar). STATUS.md and UI-MIGRATION-PLAN still use pre-rename engine names R9D9/R3D3/R1D1 for JT90/JT30/JT10; STATUS.md marks them ✅ registered while code-audit-jan23.md calls the same engines 'old… not yet modernized'.
- Reverb status is contradictory, including within one file: CLAUDE.md documents reverb as a fully working effect with presets; TOOLING-STATUS.md's summary lists Reverb under 'Untested' but its own detail table says '❌ broken — wet and dry renders are currently bit-identical in JB01 send test'; RELEASE-NOTES says 'probably works, needs testing'. Also the algorithm is described as Freeverb-style (PLATFORM.md) vs Dattorro plate (RELEASE-NOTES).
- Send/return routing: CLAUDE.md presents sends as a working, recommended feature ('Prefer add_send + route for reverb and delay'), but code-audit-jan23.md found 'Send buses: data only — render.js uses effect chains, not sends' and 'RoutingManager exists, not used', and TOOLING-STATUS's wet==dry send-test failure suggests that finding may still hold.
- PLATFORM.md contradicts itself on session.set units: the Philosophy section shows session.set('drums.kick.decay', 0.75) (engine units) while the engineering memo shows session.set('jt90.kick.decay', 70) (producer units); 2026-02-17.md confirms this bit real users ('Was mixing the two = wrong levels'). ParamSystem examples in PLATFORM.md also say get() 'returns engine value (0-1)' while the tweak/get_param tool docs promise producer units.
- STATUS.md ('Known Issues: None currently blocking', everything ✅) contradicts TOOLING-STATUS.md (JB202 needs tuning, reverb broken, 7 areas untested) and RELEASE-NOTES' 'Probably Broken' section (sampler, EQ, sidechain, filter, automation). STATUS.md is dated 2025-01-23 and is the stalest status doc; TOOLING-STATUS (2026-02-21) supersedes it.
- code-audit-jan23.md says 'No formal interface contract — instruments are duck-typed', but PLATFORM.md documents validateInterface() running automatically at registration and tests/test-interface-contract.js exists — the audit is stale on this point (the gap it flagged was later closed).
- JB200-CUSTOM-DSP-PLAN.md is superseded: it plans fixing cross-platform drift via PeriodicWave harmonics on JB200; the shipped solution was JB202 with fully custom pure-JS DSP (PolyBLEP oscillators, custom biquad), which CLAUDE.md documents as the current design.
- UI migration state is ambiguous: UI-MIGRATION-PLAN.md says delete ui.tsx and remove Ink after migration, but both ui.tsx and terminal-ui.ts exist in the repo, CLAUDE.md 'Architecture' still lists 'ui.tsx — Ink-based terminal UI' (and PLATFORM.md's file tree lists only ui.tsx), and RELEASE-NOTES credits 'UI: Ink'.
- PLATFORM.md checklist says 'All three test files should pass' but tests/ contains 8 test files — stale relative to the test suite it mandates.
- CLAUDE.md music-knowledge section self-contradicts: 'unified music knowledge — 45 genres and 1 artist profile' followed two paragraphs later by 'Artists: Jeff Mills, Hannes Bieger' (two).
- PLATFORM.md file tree still shows presets/jb200/kits and presets/jb200/sequences (legacy jb200 folder name) while CLAUDE.md's preset architecture says presets/{synth}/kits with JB202 canonical; RELEASE-ENGINEERING.md's file table references genres.json as the bundled genre knowledge, but CLAUDE.md says library.json is canonical (genres.json is raw source in musical-knowledge/).
- PLATFORM.md describes core/library.js as 'Save/load projects' while CLAUDE.md describes core/library.js as the music-knowledge injector (detectLibraryKeys/buildLibraryContext) — same file, two unrelated documented purposes; at least one description is wrong or the file has two jobs undocumented in either place.

- The 'no bespoke code' rule (R5) is acknowledged as aspirational by the project's own release notes: 'In practice, we've written a lot of bespoke per-instrument code' and 'What we actually did: Wrote add_jb01, add_jb202, add_jt10, add_jt30, add_jt90…' (RELEASE-NOTES-v0.1.md 'Reality Check') — the contract and the shipped tool surface openly disagree.
